steps: Unpack & pre-fit

Check for shipping damage and confirm the hardware kit (LP conversion kit, conversion notice plate, rock wool, remote and wall bracket, 4 AA and 3 AAA batteries, screen guidelines). Remove the pallet bracket screws, release the glass frame with the Latch Tool, and level the firebox in place with the corner bolts (max. 1/2" adjustment).
Prepare fireplace & chimney

Solid fuel-burning masonry or factory-built fireplace only. Clean the flue (a Level II inspection may be needed), repair any damage, and never share the flue with another appliance. Factory-built: remove doors, screens, grates and the damper.

• Clean the existing chimney flue thoroughly; a Level II inspection may be needed (see NFPA 211). Don't install into a damaged chimney or one containing combustible construction materials; repair first.
  • Don't remove bricks or mortar. Masonry or steel may come out of the smoke shelf and damper frame area for the liners if that doesn't weaken the structure.
  • Never connect to a chimney or flue serving any other appliance.
  • If the fireplace was modified, fix the metal Fireplace Conversion Notice Plate to the back wall of the firebox.
  • Factory-built: remove glass doors, screen rails and mesh, fuel grates and the damper assembly (two 3" liners must pass); keep removed parts. Don't cut out sheet metal. A gas access hole of 1 1/2" or less may be drilled in the lower sides or bottom, then sealed with noncombustible insulation.
Run the chimney liners

Cut both 3" liners, label the exhaust at both ends, drop them from the top, seal the termination kit with high-temperature sealant and fit the direct vent cap. Trim so the ends hang approx. 15" above the fireplace floor; block off the flue if the intake stops short of the cap.
Gas connection + pressure test

Connect at the valve on the left side and leak-test with soapy water or an electronic sensor, never a flame. Check inlet and manifold pressure at the valve test points with the regulator at its highest setting.

• Supply connects to the valve on the left side (facing the unit). Line min. 3/8" or sized to hold pressure at any input. A 36" length of 3/8" flexible gas line is supplied; where flex lines aren't permitted, a 3/8" iron nipple and union is recommended.
  • An integrated gas cock sits just upstream of the valve. Operate it with the Latch Tool: pull toward you to open, push back to close. A T-handle gas cock is required in Massachusetts (248 CMR).
  • Propane: use propane-resistant sealing compounds. Leak-test with soapy water or an electronic gas sensor, never an open flame.
  • Close the gas cock to isolate the appliance during supply-piping pressure tests at or above 1/2 psig.
  • Manometer on the inlet and OUT (manifold) test points on the valve face, regulator at its highest setting. Inlet must not exceed 14.0" WC.
Fuel conversion / high altitude
Before the insert goes in: LP kit 157784 (injectors, pilot injector, regulator tower, baffle wing, labels), or the high-altitude orifices above 2000 ft. Leak-test and pressure-test again.

Do this before the insert goes into the fireplace or the surround goes on. Gas off, power off, glass frame removed.

  1. Push both air shutter cables fully in; lift out the two support shelves and the burner.
  2. Swap the burner injectors (1/2" wrench or deep-well socket) and the pilot injector (7/16" wrench); aim the pilot hood directly forward at the burner ports and flame sensor.
  3. LP only: remove the upper baffle wing.
  4. Replace the regulator tower on the valve (two Torx screws; reconnect the IFC lead).
  5. Apply the conversion labels, reinstall the burner (shutters and trays fully forward), then leak-test, pressure-test and run the initial system check.

Above 2000 ft: fit the high-altitude orifices from Table 1 and apply the completed conversion notice label to the rating plate; the air shutters may need adjusting.

Note: p. 16 says to apply conversion label A to the base of the valve compartment; p. 18 says to apply it to the right side compartment adjacent to the rating plate.
Connect vent & set in place

Vacuum the fireplace, attach the liners to the Vent Adaptor by its exhaust ID (exhaust right, intake left; screws or duct clamps, no sealant), lock the adaptor onto the firebox and push the insert fully home. Route the blower cord to power.
Initial system check

Fit 3 AAA in the remote, connect 120 VAC, purge the line, set the burner switch to REMOTE and pick IPI or CPI, then press Power: the burner lights on Low. Pilot flames steady, blue with yellow edges, 1" long, engulfing the top 1/4" of the sensor.
Panels & log set
Optional brick or reflective glass panels first, then the logs in numbered order. Rock wool in small tufts across the front of the burner base only; keep burner ports and the pilot area clear.

Brick panel kits 157877 (Traditional Red), 157878 (Brownstone) and 158082 (Fluted), or reflective glass kit 157879, go in before the logs. Panels are very fragile; handle glass panels with the cotton gloves supplied. Then set the logs in numbered order as the figures show, starting with the rear log on the two pegs of the rear burner skirt.

Use the rock wool sparingly: small tufts across the front of the burner base only. Never at the rear of the burner base or over burner ports, and keep the pilot area and carry-over ports clear.

Note: the accessory list on p. 4 gives the log set part numbers as Traditional #158094 and Beach Fire #158095; the log set pages give Traditional 157896 (p. 22) and Beach Fire 158093 (p. 24).
Air shutters & flame picture

First firing: shutters fully open (cables pushed in), both burners on HIGH for 15 - 20 minutes, then adjust in 1/8" - 1/4" steps; left cable front burner, right cable rear. No soot or smoke; LP usually needs more air than NG.
Backer plate & surround overlay
Last, after all checks: backer plate (ten M6 x 8 screws) or hidden hanger brackets, then hang the overlay with its integrated safety screen. Keep a minimum 3/4" air space behind the overlay.

• Standard backer plate: ten M6 x 8 phillips screws, attached loosely, then tightened in an alternating pattern.
  • Trimmable backer plate (22 ga.): scribe and trim, engage it on the hidden hanger brackets (Kit 157888, included), then tighten.
  • No backer plate: Hidden Hanger Bracket Kit 157888 is required to hang the overlay.
  • Keep a minimum 3/4" air space between the overlay and the backer plate or fireplace face. Don't recess the firebox past the front lip of the top safety bracket or move the hanger brackets.
  • Overlays ship assembled with the safety barrier screen; remove the four plastic joint shims from the Brown Majolica frame. Factory-built: don't block any fireplace ventilation openings.

panels.title: Insufficient gas pressure
items: Small pilot flame → poor pilot rectification and/or frequent burner outages
Little variation in flame picture between HI and LO
Not enough gas for more than one appliance → nuisance outages or gas surges

panels.title: Excessive gas pressure
items: Permanent valve damage → complete appliance shutdown
Pilot flame too large → flame sensor overheats → shutdown
Sooting from impingement and/or incorrect fuel-to-air mix

panels.title: Flame picture / air shutters
items: Very long yellow flames, soot on logs, firebox walls or cap → too little combustion air
Very blue, transparent, weak "anemic" flames → too much air
Soot or smoke → check log placement first, then open the air shutter

panels.title: Weak draft / IPI starts
items: Warm weather, extreme cold, long vent run or high wind → IPI trouble; run in CPI mode
Steep roof, nearby trees, windy site → weak draft or downdrafts; raise the vent or fit a high-wind cap
Pilot fails twice, or burner flame lost a third time → lock-out (3 blinks)

codes: Pilot failed twice or flame lost a third time; clear the lock-out

light.title: Lighting the fireplace
light.html:
Your fireplace has an igniter that lights the pilot for you. Never try to light the pilot by hand. The burner switch is in the right-side control compartment, with the battery box.

  1. Read the gas-smell steps under Safety first.
  2. Set the burner switch to OFF.
  3. Wait five minutes to clear out any gas. Then smell for gas, including near the floor. If you smell gas, stop and follow the gas-smell steps.
  4. Set the burner switch to REMOTE.
  5. With the remote off, press Mode, then the Up or Down arrow to choose CPI. The pilot will light.
  6. Press the remote's On/Off button to light the burner.

The burner always starts on Low for a 2-minute warm-up, while the red light on the switch box blinks in groups of 4. Then the flame goes to your last setting.

IPI or CPI?

IPI (the default) lights the pilot only when you call for heat, and it goes out when the burner stops. CPI keeps the pilot lit for up to 7 days; with no call for heat in that time, it goes out and switches back to IPI. CPI helps in warm, very cold or windy weather and with long vents, and it cuts fog on the glass. With the pilot always on, don't use cleaning products with combustible vapors nearby.

Won't light? Turn off the gas to the appliance and call your service technician or gas supplier.

remote.title: Using the remote
remote.html:
The remote and the fireplace are paired at the factory. Leave the burner switch on REMOTE for everyday use. The fireplace beeps once to confirm each command.

  • On/Off turns the burner on and off. It lights on Low for a 2-minute warm-up, then returns to your last setting.
  • Up / Down steps through six flame levels. It also sets the temperature, fan speed and lamp brightness.
  • Thermostat cycles three choices: on (the remote works as a room thermostat), Smart (the flame turns down as the room nears your set temperature) and off (you set the flame yourself).
  • Mode picks what you're adjusting: pilot mode (CPI or IPI), the front burner (Split Flow icon), the fan or the accent lamp.

Child lock: press Mode and Up together to lock, Mode and Down to unlock. Room temperature: with the remote off, press Thermostat and Mode together; each press switches between Fahrenheit and Celsius.

Won't use the fireplace for a long time? Set the burner switch to OFF.

Thermostat warning: on thermostat control the fireplace can come on by itself, and it may be very hot even when the burner looks off. Keep the remote where children can't reach it. The included wall bracket helps.

sounds.title: First fires, sounds and fog
sounds.html:
Smoke and odor at first

The paint and log set cure during the first hours of use, which gives off some odor and visible smoke. The fumes are non-toxic but can bother babies, young children, pregnant women, older people, pets and anyone with breathing problems. Open doors and windows and use a fan to bring in fresh air. Once your installer has checked every heat level, run it on low for 2-4 hours, then on high for 2-4 hours.

A soft "woof" or "thud"

A muffled woof or thud when the burner lights or goes out is normal. If it gets unusually loud or disturbing, stop using the fireplace and call a qualified service technician.

Beeps and the fan

One beep confirms a remote command. A double beep when you press a button means a low battery. The fan keeps running for 12 minutes after the burner shuts off.

Fog on the glass

Condensation forms on the glass at each cold start and clears as the glass warms. CPI pilot mode reduces it. A white, powdery film after the first fires is different: clean it off soon (see Clean the glass).

A gas smell is not normal. Don't touch switches or phones. See Safety for what to do.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
After the first few fires, a white, powdery film shows up on the inside of the glass as the paint and logs cure. Clean it off with a non-abrasive household glass cleaner or warm water. Left on, it can permanently etch the glass.

Everyday care

  • Some condensation and a light film of particles on the inside of the glass are normal.
  • Wipe with a damp, soft cloth and polish with a dry, soft towel. A ceramic glass cleaner is fine too.
  • Never clean the glass while it's hot.
  • Don't use abrasive or ammonia-based cleaners, and take care not to scratch it.
Scratched, cracked or broken glass? Don't use the fireplace. Scratches weaken the glass, so a scratched panel should be replaced, only with Jøtul part 157894 and only by a licensed or qualified service person.

Don't slam or strike the glass. It can shatter if something hits it.

trouble.title: Won't light, or the light is blinking
trouble.html:
A small red light on the switch box blinks to tell you what the control is doing:

1 blinkRemote command received
2 blinksLow battery
3 blinksLock-out
4 blinksWarm-up at minimum flame

Clearing a lock-out

It locks out if the pilot fails to light on its second try, or if the burner flame is lost a third time. In IPI or CPI mode, turn it OFF for 5 seconds, ON for 5 seconds, then OFF again and wait for the control's beep. No beep? Repeat until you hear it.

Hard starts in some weather

Warm weather, extreme cold, a long vent or high wind can weaken the draft and upset IPI starts. Running in CPI mode keeps the pilot lit and helps.

Remote stopped working?

Put three fresh AAA batteries in. Set the burner switch to REMOTE and press the black PRG button on the switch box; it beeps three times. Within 10 seconds, press ON on the remote. Three beeps confirm it's paired.

Still won't operate? Turn off the gas to the appliance: set the remote thermostat to its lowest setting, set the burner switch to OFF, and disconnect power if service is needed. Then call your service technician or gas supplier.

fan.title: Blower and accent lamp
fan.html:
A built-in blower helps move heat into the room. You control it from the remote.

  • On, off and speed: press Mode until the fan icon shows, then use Up or Down to turn it on, off, or pick one of six speeds. One beep confirms.
  • Why it speeds up: about 5 minutes after it starts, the fan runs at its highest speed, then settles back to your setting.
  • Why it keeps running: it runs for 12 minutes after the burner turns off.
  • Smart thermostat: while Smart is on, you can't set the fan speed by hand.

Accent lamp

With the remote on, press Mode to the lamp icon. Up turns it on and the arrows set the brightness; Down turns it off. The replacement bulb is part 222943 (130V, 50W). Handle it with gloves, because skin oil makes bulbs fail early.

The blower and lamp don't work in a power outage. The burner still does, on battery backup.

The blower has a three-prong grounding plug. Plug it straight into a grounded three-prong outlet, and never cut off the grounding prong.

power.title: Power outages and batteries
power.html:
The fireplace runs on 120-volt house current, which powers the electronic ignition, the blower and the accent lamp.

Back-up battery box4 × 1.5v AA
Remote3 × 1.5v AAA

In a power outage

Put the four AA batteries in the back-up battery box in the right-side compartment. The burner then keeps working from the remote. The blower and accent lamp stay off until power returns.

Don't leave the AA batteries in the box permanently. The box will corrode.

Changing the AA batteries

  1. Disconnect electrical power to the fireplace.
  2. Remove the cast iron overlay.
  3. Press the cover plate tabs to open the battery box.
  4. Fit four new AA batteries, matching the polarity marks on the box.

A low battery shows up as a double beep when you send a command from the remote, and the remote's screen has a low-battery indicator.

safety.title: Safety and gas smell
safety.html:
If you smell gas

  • Put out any open flame and open windows.
  • Don't light any appliance, touch any electrical switch, or use any phone in your building.
  • Call your gas supplier right away from outside the house. If you can't reach them, call the fire department.

Around the fireplace

  • The glass and surfaces get very hot. Keep everyone back, and supervise young children in the room. A child guard or safety gate is recommended if anyone at risk lives with you.
  • The safety screen on the front reduces burns from the hot glass and must stay in place. If it's damaged, replace it before using the fireplace.
  • Keep clothing and anything flammable away, and never store or use gasoline or other flammable liquids nearby.
  • Burn only natural gas or propane, never wood, paper, cardboard or coal.
  • If any part has been under water, don't use the fireplace. Immediately call a qualified service technician to inspect the fireplace and to replace any part of the control system and any gas control that has been under water.
Note: p. 6 says to replace a damaged safety screen only with Jøtul barrier part 225731; the parts list on p. 42 gives 225731 for the cast iron overlay's screen and 225985 for the steel overlay's screen.

In Massachusetts, a carbon monoxide detector must be installed in the same room.

service.title: Cleaning and annual service
service.html:
Have a qualified service technician inspect the fireplace and its venting before use and at least once a year.

Your part

  • Monthly: vacuum the controls area under the firebox, more often if you have pets. Make sure the burner and firebox are cold first.
  • Keep the control compartments free of dust, and keep the area around the fireplace clear of anything that burns.

Once a year

  • Vacuum the firebox, using a brush attachment on the logs.
  • Clear debris from the burner ports, especially the pilot carry-over ports, and check the pilot for corrosion.
  • Check the glass gasket for wear or stiffness and make sure it still seals. A good seal keeps combustion gases out of the room.

Soot or smoke?

You shouldn't see any. Check that the logs are placed correctly. If soot or smoke continues, the air shutters may need adjusting, which is a job for a qualified service technician only.

Turn off the gas and disconnect power before any service work, including battery changes.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Jøtul's limited warranty covers the original retail purchaser, starting from the date of purchase.

Cast iron, steel doors, surround components, firebox5 years
Burner, burner treatments, firebox panels2 years
Enamel finish (peeling or fading)2 years
Gas and electrical parts (controls, plumbing, valve, blower)1 year

Making a claim

  • Contact your nearest authorized Jøtul dealer.
  • Jøtul must get notice within 60 days of when the defect was first discovered, or reasonably could have been.
  • Keep your dated sales receipt as proof of purchase. The warranty isn't transferable.

Not covered, for example

  • Wear parts: paint, lamp bulbs, gaskets and glass (unless damaged by thermal stress).
  • Incorrect installation, or unauthorized modification or repair.
  • Enamel damage from misuse, travel time, and damage in transit.
The warranty is void if installation or service is done by someone other than an authorized installer, service agency or gas supplier.

specInlet.title: Inlet (supply) pressure
specInlet.html:
Natural gas5.0 – 7.0 in. WC
Propane11.0 – 14.0 in. WC
The p. 4 specifications table also prints kPa beside these figures: NG 5.0 WC (1.00 kPa) and 7.0 WC (1.74 kPa); LP 11.0 WC (3.00 kPa) and 14.0 WC (3.48 kPa). The 1.00 and 3.00 kPa figures don't match their in. WC values; the in. WC figures match the p. 15 pressure chart.

Read at the inlet test point on the face of the control valve (the arrow embossed on the valve), with the valve regulator at its highest setting. The manual's tools list calls for an external regulator for propane only.

Don't let inlet pressure exceed 14.0" WC (or 1/2 psig): serious valve damage may result. Close the internal gas cock to isolate the appliance during supply-piping pressure tests at or above 1/2 psig.

specManifold.title: Manifold pressure
specManifold.html:
Natural gas1.6 – 3.5 in. WC
Propane6.4 – 10.0 in. WC
The p. 4 specifications table also prints kPa beside these figures that don't match them: NG 1.6 WC (0.27 kPa) and 3.5 WC (0.95 kPa); LP 6.4 WC (0.72 kPa) and 10.0 WC (2.74 kPa). The in. WC figures match the p. 15 pressure chart, which gives in. WC only.

Read at the OUT test point on the valve face, regulator at its highest setting. Pilot flames: steady, blue at the hood with traces of yellow at the edges, projecting 1" and fully engulfing the top 1/4" of the flame sensor. Pilot adjustment screw is on the valve body; qualified gas technician only.

specVent.title: Venting
specVent.html:
Vent through the chimney with a pair of 3" flexible aluminum liners listed for gas appliances. Exhaust (right collar, facing the unit) runs the full chimney length to the termination cap. Intake (left collar) runs through the damper area into at least the first flue tile (U.S. only), or the full length. In Canada both run full length and connect to the termination kit.

Cap height above unit10 ft min · 35 ft max
Liner diameter3" (no less, no greater, except the LP note)
Horizontal runsNot permitted
Liner endsapprox. 15" above the fireplace floor
Note: p. 10 recommends a 4" exhaust liner for LP vent runs greater than 10'; the venting figures on pp. 11 and 12 say to adapt the exhaust to 4" dia. for LP at max. height.
  • Intake not connected to the cap: a noncombustible (metal) block-off plate above the unit, below the end of the intake (normally the damper area); factory-built fireplaces need a minimum 6 foot intake length.
  • Label the exhaust duct at both ends to avoid cross-venting.
  • High-wind termination cap recommended for all IPI appliances (M&G DuraVent wind screen #46DVA-VWG).
  • 3" to 4" collar adaptors: ICC TM-I34; DuraVent 3GVBTI4 P/N 810004525.
  • Use one approved vent manufacturer's parts only. Liners may not be exposed to any living space; never connect to a flue serving another appliance.

review.notes: Catalog BTU, efficiency, vent size, mobile-home approval and IPI/CPI ignition all match the manual (pp. 1, 4, 10). Not checkable from the text: weight (156 lb) and heating area (2,000 sq ft) are not stated; the firebox dimension drawing (Fig. 5.1, p. 7) shows callouts that include 19 3/4", 29 1/2" and 15 1/8" (the catalog height/width/depth), but the text doesn't tie them to labels, so they aren't transcribed. Log placement (pp. 22-26) is figure-based; the Beach Fire rock captions (p. 25) use numbers that don't match the parts list, and rock part numbers 226385/226386 can't be matched to #8/#9 from the text. Smart Start: the p. 33 flowchart shows 15-second relight warm-ups for later rectification losses, while the text (pp. 32-33) gives a 2-minute pilot-only warm-up plus 2 minutes at minimum flame for losses #2 and #3; the guide doesn't describe those timings. Minor discrepancies not flagged in drawers: high-altitude standard printed as CAN/CGA 2.17-M-17 (cover) vs CAN/CSA 2.17-M91 (p. 4), and the chimney-as-air-intake notices cite ANSI Z21.88-2014 (p. 10) vs Z21.88-1999 (p. 12); the certification line lists only ANSI Z21.88-2016 · CSA 2.33-2016, which the cover and p. 4 agree on. Valve called SIT Proflame 885 (p. 16) vs Sit 886 Modulating Valve (p. 32). The approved vent manufacturer list (p. 44) names the 'GI 635 DV IPI'. The wiring diagram (p. 45) labels the blower and accent lamp 'Optional', while p. 31 calls the 120 cfm blower integral. T-handle gas cock 'may be required' in Massachusetts (p. 2) vs 'is required' per 248 CMR (p. 14); the step drawer uses the p. 14 wording. Metric-only mismatches (hearth width 3 1/8" given as 10.5 cm in the p. 8 text and 8 cm in Fig. 5.3; high-altitude band 611 - 1170 m in Table 1, p. 19, vs 610 - 1370 m elsewhere): the guide uses inches and feet only. The lighting instructions (p. 47) and part of p. 34 are partly garbled in the text layer (shifted font); decoded as 'Wait five (5) minutes to clear out any gas', 'Set the Burner Switch to REMOTE' and 'Within 10 seconds'. Lock-out reset says 'key to OFF / ON' without naming the switch or remote key; the owner drawer keeps it neutral. The manual's own page cross-references are often off (e.g. 'Sect. 8.1, page 25'); physical pages are used throughout. Gas-cock isolation wording (close it during supply-piping tests at or above 1/2 psig, p. 14) is given as printed. The battery-replacement steps (p. 37) mention only the cast iron overlay. Website check (Oct 12): weight and heating capacity aren't in the manual text; the website's height, width and depth equal the Fig. 5.1 callouts, so no note. The product bullet 'up to 64% heat control turn down' isn't a figure the guide shows (the p. 40 parts list names the valve 'NG / 30% TD'), so it gets no note.
